blocks.text: Setting up Chrome for customer support agents on Mac

Your browser is your primary workspace. Start by creating a dedicated Chrome profile for your support work. Go to the top right corner, click your profile icon, and select Add. This keeps your bookmarks, extensions, and history separate from your personal life. It prevents you from accidentally sharing personal info in a screenshot or a screen share session.

Pin your most used tabs to the left. Right-click any open tab and select Pin. These tabs stay there even when you close and reopen Chrome. This is perfect for your help desk dashboard, your internal knowledge base, and your team communication tool. You save time by not having to search for these pages every morning.

Support agents often have dozens of tabs open. Use the tab search feature to find what you need. Press ⌘ + ⇧ + A to see a list of all open tabs across your windows. Type a keyword to narrow it down. You can also use ⌘ + 1 through ⌘ + 8 to jump to specific tabs. ⌘ + 9 always takes you to the last tab.
If you have too many tabs, use Tab Groups. Right-click a tab and select Add tab to new group. You can name the group and color-code it. This keeps your screen clean and your focus sharp.

blocks.text: Lazur lives in the notch of your Mac. It sees what you see when you hold the shortcut. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. If you are stuck on a complex ticket, ask Lazur to explain the text on the page. It reads the screen and answers out loud. You do not need to switch apps or copy and paste content into another tool.

Typing the same responses over and over is exhausting. Hold the fn key to dictate text directly into your ticket reply box. Lazur formats the text for you. You can dictate a quick summary or a detailed technical answer. It is faster than typing and helps you keep up with your ticket queue. You can also use clipboard slots to store common snippets.

When a ticket requires deep research, you might open five different help articles. Instead of reading them all, use Lazur. Ask it to research a topic. It opens its own Chrome tabs, reads the pages, and summarizes the findings for you. You get a report without the manual labor of switching between tabs and synthesizing the data yourself.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for Chrome on Mac

items: ⌘ + L: Jump to the address bar
⌘ + ⇧ + T: Reopen the last closed tab
⌘ + F: Find text on the current page

blocks.text: Mastering these shortcuts will change how you interact with your browser. You keep your hands on the keyboard more often. This is a small change that adds up to hours saved each week.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in Chrome?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate apps for you. It points at things on your screen and guides you through steps, but you are the one who performs the clicks.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my screen data?
faq.answer: No. Lazur only looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut. The screenshot is sent to AI providers to answer your question and is not stored or used to train models.

faq.question: Is Lazur available on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is currently built only for macOS on Apple silicon and Intel chips.
